claimText: Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria is the public-facing policy initiative.
approvedPublicWording: Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria is the public-facing policy initiative.
evidenceSummary: Recorded in the repository README and the evidence-register governance documentation as the public-facing initiative name.
limitations: This record identifies the initiative branding and governance position only.
reviewTrigger: Review if initiative branding or governance structure changes.

claimText: Dan Sonsie is the founder of Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria.
approvedPublicWording: Dan Sonsie is the founder of Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria.
evidenceSummary: The founder designation is recorded in the governed register documentation for project governance purposes.
limitations: This record is limited to founder attribution within project governance materials.
reviewTrigger: Review if governance records are formally amended.
notes: Founder attribution is treated as a governed internal record.

claimText: Dan Sonsie is the evidence custodian for the Claims and Evidence Register.
approvedPublicWording: Dan Sonsie is the evidence custodian for the Claims and Evidence Register.
evidenceSummary: The evidence-custodian role is explicitly recorded in the evidence README, register document and ADR.
limitations: This record governs custodianship and does not by itself approve any specific claim for publication.
reviewTrigger: Review if register governance roles change.
notes: Custodianship remains separate from publication approval decisions.

claimText: Sonsie Enterprises Pty Ltd is the nominated owner of the website, source code, evidence architecture, documentation and associated intellectual property, subject to any later express written agreement.
approvedPublicWording: Sonsie Enterprises Pty Ltd is recorded as the nominated owner of the website, source code, evidence architecture, documentation and associated intellectual property, subject to any later express written agreement.
evidenceSummary: Recorded as the approved governance and ownership position in the evidence README, register document, ADR and existing rights notice.
limitations: This is an owner-declared governance record for project administration and publication control. It is not recorded as independent legal advice or an independently verified legal conclusion.
prohibitedWording: The ownership position has been independently verified as a legal conclusion.
requiredNextEvidence: Maintain any later express written agreement as a controlled documentary source if governance or ownership designations change.
reviewTrigger: Review if a later written agreement changes asset or IP ownership designations.
notes: Public wording must remain cautious and governance-based.

claimText: The internal register and filtered public register serve different publication and confidentiality purposes.
approvedPublicWording: The full register is maintained internally, with only approved publication-safe material intended for public release.
evidenceSummary: The evidence README, ADR and governed register document all state that the complete register remains internal and only filtered publication-safe material may be surfaced publicly.
limitations: A public release still requires separate publication review and filtering decisions for each record.
reviewTrigger: Review if publication controls or confidentiality rules are amended.
notes: Supports the distinction between internal governance records and filtered public material.

claimText: Victoria’s building reform program identifies expanded practitioner registration as part of its reform direction.
approvedPublicWording: Current Victorian building reform identifies expanded practitioner registration as part of the reform direction.
evidenceSummary: The current Building Reform page and the 2025 Building Statement both describe expanded practitioner registration as part of Victoria’s reform architecture.
limitations: This records a current reform direction only. It does not identify advanced residential carpenters as a proposed registration category.
reviewTrigger: Review if Victorian Government reform material is updated or superseded.
notes: Used as system-level context, not endorsement.

claimText: The 2025 Building Statement identifies clear authorised work scopes, objective competence benchmarks, standardised practical-experience requirements and assessment as principles for an enhanced practitioner-registration system.
approvedPublicWording: The 2025 Building Statement describes clearer authorised work scope, objective competence, qualifications, experience and assessment as part of an enhanced practitioner-registration system.
evidenceSummary: The Building Statement records system-design principles linking registration settings to scope, competence, qualifications, experience and assessment.
limitations: This is a practitioner-registration design principle. It is not a published commitment to a new advanced carpenter class.
reviewTrigger: Review if the Building Statement is replaced or materially amended.
notes: Supports capability-first alignment with government reform architecture.

claimText: Current Victorian Building Reform material states that the registration framework will be expanded to broaden the practitioners required to be registered.
approvedPublicWording: Current Victorian Building Reform material states that the registration framework will be expanded to broaden the practitioners required to be registered.
evidenceSummary: The current government reform page presents practitioner-registration expansion as part of the live reform program.
limitations: The published material does not list advanced carpenters as a proposed category.
prohibitedWording: Government is creating a new advanced carpenter registration.
reviewTrigger: Review if the live Building Reform page changes its registration wording.

claimText: Current reform material states that registration can prescribe qualifications and experience and restrict regulated work to qualified, competent practitioners.
approvedPublicWording: Current reform material links practitioner registration to defined qualifications, experience and competence requirements for regulated work.
evidenceSummary: The current reform material and Building Statement both describe registration settings that connect regulated work with prescribed qualifications, experience and competence.
limitations: This is general practitioner-registration architecture. It does not settle the form of any advanced residential carpentry pathway.
reviewTrigger: Review if qualifications-and-experience settings are updated in official reform material.

claimText: Building consultants and site supervisors are specifically identified for consideration under expanded practitioner registration settings.
approvedPublicWording: Current reform material specifically identifies categories such as building consultants and site supervisors within expanded practitioner-registration settings.
evidenceSummary: Current government reform material identifies site supervisors and building consultants within expanded registration settings.
limitations: Advanced carpenters are not currently identified on the published reform page as a proposed new category.
prohibitedWording: Government is creating a new advanced carpenter registration.
reviewTrigger: Review if official reform material adds or removes named practitioner classes.
notes: Important limitation record for public wording control.

claimText: Victoria’s current building reform includes measures intended to improve consumer understanding of practitioner roles.
approvedPublicWording: Current Victorian reform includes measures intended to improve consumer understanding of practitioner roles and responsibilities.
evidenceSummary: The reform material and Building Statement both connect registration reform and consumer protection to clearer practitioner roles and accountability.
limitations: This is general reform context. It is not published government support for the RRC proposal.
reviewTrigger: Review if official reform material materially changes its consumer-protection framing.
notes: Supports consumer role-comprehension testing in the pilot materials.

claimText: Building manuals are required for specified new Class 1b, 2 and 3 buildings from 1 February 2027 under current Victorian reform settings.
approvedPublicWording: Current Victorian reform material introduces building-manual requirements for specified new Class 1b, 2 and 3 buildings from 1 February 2027.
evidenceSummary: The current government reform material uses building manuals as a persistent-building-information measure for specified building classes.
limitations: Do not represent this as a Class 1a residential renovation requirement.
prohibitedWording: Building manuals already apply to Class 1a residential renovation work.
reviewTrigger: Review if building-manual commencement dates or class coverage change.
notes: Used only as a persistent-record context point, with a strict class limitation.

claimText: Current Victorian building reform provides a relevant policy context for considering whether advanced residential renovation carpentry should be evaluated as a defined practitioner function, endorsement or assessed competency stream.
approvedPublicWording: Current Victorian building reform provides a relevant policy context for evaluating advanced residential renovation carpentry within a framework of defined scope, competence, experience and accountability.
evidenceSummary: The reform material supports a capability-first interpretation because it focuses on practitioner scope, competence, experience, accountability and consumer protection rather than pre-committing to one statutory vehicle.
limitations: This is a governed interpretation. It is not verified government support for RRC or for a new advanced carpenter registration category.
requiredNextEvidence: Maintain this as interpretation only unless future official material expressly addresses advanced residential carpentry.
reviewTrigger: Review if official Victorian reform material expressly addresses advanced carpentry or a comparable category.
notes: Key supported interpretation for capability-first / vehicle-second positioning.
